clue.text: Witness former PM dropping a couple of Es somewhere in Washington

indicators.note: dropping means these letters fall out of the combined witness-and-premier string

parts.note: to witness is to see
Clement Attlee was the British Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951
two letter Es

explanation.surface: A witness watches an ex-prime minister mangling his speech somewhere in Washington State.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes one E from SEE and the final E from ATTLEE, leaving SEATTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is the largest city in the US state of Washington, so it is a place there.

clue.text: French bloke outside fancy cinema knocked over inspector

indicators.note: knocked over means toppled, so in a down clue the whole is read upwards
outside means the name goes round the cinema brand

parts.note: René is a French man's name
IMAX is a large-format cinema system

explanation.surface: A Frenchman outside a smart cinema knocked over an official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' gives RENIMAXE; 'knocked over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner is someone who inspects or tests, so is an inspector.

clue.text: Curtail reporting of case eight

indicators.note: reporting of means speaking the words, so we enter what they sound like

parts.note: a trunk is a large travel case, followed by the number eight

explanation.surface: A legal case number eight being cut short in the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a lawsuit but is a piece of luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: To truncate is to shorten by cutting off a part, which is to curtail.

clue.text: Pericles revised, six boxed; it's rather casually paid

indicators.note: boxed means the shuffled letters enclose the Roman numeral
revised means the Greek statesman's name is rewritten in a new order

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A revised edition of Pericles with six of something boxed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' reorders the statesman's name to make LIPSERCE, and 'boxed' then puts the numeral inside it before the final CE.
explanation.definitionFit: We speak of paying lip service: expressing support only in words, without real commitment.

clue.text: Pop about to be fitted with oxygen line

indicators.note: to be fitted with means the abbreviation takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Dad is about to go on an oxygen line in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like Dad but means a fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cola is a fizzy soft drink, and pop is the informal word for such drinks.

clue.text: One who works their way to the top?

definitions.text: One who works their way to the top?

parts.words: One who works their way to the top?
parts.note: reads like an ambitious careerist, but describes a Himalayan guide and porter who climbs to mountain summits

explanation.surface: An ambitious person climbing the corporate ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: The career-climber reading misleads; the top is a literal Himalayan peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas, the Nepalese people, are famed as mountaineering guides who carry loads up to Everest's summit.

clue.text: Be chairperson, in the days before spin?

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
side is spin put on a ball in billiards or snooker

explanation.surface: Chairing meetings in the days before political spin doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' is snooker and billiards spin, called side in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside is to take the chair and run a meeting, so be chairperson.

clue.text: Drug firm, one from Germany, located in the outskirts of Dundee

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: located in means the German word sits inside the outer letters
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: ein is German for one

explanation.surface: A drug company, with a German partner, is based on the edge of Dundee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'located in' sets the German word between the first and last letters of Dundee.
explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is an opiate painkiller derived from morphine, so it is a drug.

clue.text: Behold threesome featuring husband (Aylesbury's number one womaniser)

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: featuring means the group of three now includes the other letters within it

parts.note: a trio is a group of three

indicators.note: number one means only the first letter of the town's name is used

explanation.surface: A racy tale of a threesome and a husband in Aylesbury, starring the town's leading philanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featuring' puts HA (H plus the A heading Aylesbury) inside TRIO after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario is the seducer in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent, and his name became a byword for a philanderer.

clue.text: Move clumsily, having a lump hampering bandages

indicators.note: bandages is a verb here: the outer words wrap round and hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Someone with a painful lump walks awkwardly because their bandages get in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bandages' reads as a noun but is the verb that holds the answer within 'having a lump hampering'.
explanation.definitionFit: To galumph, Lewis Carroll's coinage, is to move in a heavy, ungainly, lumbering way.

clue.text: Female adult, 21, left English sea area

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
the answer to clue 21, a woman's name

explanation.surface: A grown woman named after a cross-reference has left for an English stretch of sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair Isle is one of the sea areas in the BBC Shipping Forecast, the radio bulletin of weather around the British Isles.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair Isle names a region in the Shipping Forecast, the waters round the island between Orkney and Shetland.

clue.text: Twerp, fool, horrid little weed lived by here

definitions.note: Little Weed lived between the two pots in the BBC children's show Flower Pot Men

indicators.note: horrid suggests the jumbled insults are messed up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Name-calling aimed at a nasty little weed.
explanation.walkthrough: In the 1950s BBC children's programme Flower Pot Men, Bill and Ben lived in flowerpots with Little Weed growing between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowerpot is a plant container, the home of Little Weed's neighbours in that television programme.

clue.text: Blunder as royal gardens beauty pageant winner announced?

indicators.note: announced means the phrase is spoken and we enter what it sounds like

parts.note: a beauty queen is titled Miss plus her place, and Kew is the Royal Botanic Gardens in London

explanation.surface: An embarrassing slip, such as a beauty contest winner being wrongly named.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London; a pageant winner from there would be Miss Kew.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscue is a faulty stroke in snooker or billiards, extended to any blunder or mistake.

clue.text: Joey crushed fag end outside Queen's penthouse terrace

parts.note: a joey is a baby kangaroo, and roo is short for kangaroo

indicators.note: outside means the shuffled letters sit around the royal abbreviation
crushed means the letters of the stubbed cigarette are mashed into a new order

parts.note: R stands for Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A young kangaroo stamps out a cigarette end beside the Queen's luxury rooftop patio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' reorders the stub's letters as FGADEN, and 'outside' wraps that round the royal R.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof garden is a planted terrace on top of a building, typically beside a penthouse.

clue.text: Autopilot set to fly around British airport

parts.note: George is RAF slang for an aircraft's automatic pilot

indicators.note: to fly around means the letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: An autopilot is set to circle a British airport.
explanation.walkthrough: George Best Belfast City Airport is named after the Northern Irish footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: Belfast's City Airport was renamed after footballer George Best, so his name identifies an airport.

clue.text: Yarn recalled Battle of Britain pilots from Yorkshire

indicators.note: recalled suggests calling back, so the phrase is read in reverse

parts.words: Battle of Britain pilots from Yorkshire
parts.note: Churchill called the RAF fighter pilots 'the Few'; in Yorkshire dialect 'the' is shortened to t'

explanation.surface: Yorkshire airmen of 1940 being remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses T'FEW. 'Yarn' looks like a story but means thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Weft is the crosswise thread woven through the warp, so it is a kind of yarn.

clue.text: Writer Harry in Vienna to retire, laze about having collected Oscar

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the surname is read backwards

parts.note: Harry Lime is the racketeer in Vienna in the film The Third Man

indicators.note: having collected means the rearranged letters take in the radio-alphabet letter
about means the letters of the idle word are moved around

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Harry in Vienna retires to lounge about, after picking up an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retire' gives EMIL; 'about' turns the idle word into EZLA, and 'having collected' takes in the O to make EZOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Émile Zola was the French novelist of the Rougon-Macquart cycle and author of J'accuse.

clue.text: One's triggered to show anger with pent-up force

parts.note: to air something is to show it publicly

indicators.note: pent-up means held inside, so the letter is enclosed

parts.note: to rile is to anger
F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: Someone is triggered into showing rage with bottled-up force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'triggered' suggests emotional upset but means fired by a trigger.
explanation.definitionFit: An air rifle is a gun fired by pulling a trigger, using compressed air.

clue.text: To do with organs/claviers being out of tune?

indicators.note: out of tune instruments are jumbled in sound, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A question about organs and keyboard instruments playing out of tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organs' suggests musical organs next to claviers, but means body organs.
explanation.definitionFit: Visceral relates to the viscera, the internal organs of the body.

clue.text: Uplift of Village People hit entertaining a Delaware school

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the other letters go inside
uplift means raising, so in a down clue the title reads upwards

parts.note: Y.M.C.A. was a 1978 hit for the disco group Village People
DE is the postal abbreviation for Delaware

explanation.surface: A Village People hit gets a lift by entertaining a school in Delaware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplift of' turns the song title upwards to ACMY, and 'entertaining' takes in A and the state code after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a school, especially a specialised or secondary one.

clue.text: First part of Pygmalion broadcast — rambling Shaw twaddle!

parts.note: the first part of Pygmalion, PYG, said aloud is pig, and a hog is a pig

indicators.note: rambling means wandering, so the playwright's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses Shaw's Pygmalion when broadcast as rambling twaddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Pygmalion is a play by George Bernard Shaw, which makes the surface hang together.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwash is worthless nonsense, originally pig swill, so it means twaddle.

clue.text: Woman taking shelter regularly during air raids

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: A woman heads for a bomb shelter whenever the sirens sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of 'air raids'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a woman's given name, so it fits a clue asking for a woman.

clue.text: Idiot sheep milling around terminus in Reading — it holds things up on the line

definitions.text: it holds things up on the line

parts.note: a clot is a fool or idiot

indicators.note: milling around describes the flock shuffling about, so the letters are rearranged
the terminus of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A fool and some sheep wander around a railway station at Reading, where trains run on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milling around' reorders the flock's letters as HESPE. The 'line' is a washing line, not a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes peg clips wet laundry to a washing line, holding it up to dry.

clue.text: Browbeat hospital over shocking treatment placed on heads of older residents

indicators.note: over means above in a down clue, so this letter sits first
placed on means set above in a down clue, so these letters come before the rest

parts.note: ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, an electric shock treatment

indicators.note: heads of means the first letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Elderly care-home residents are bullied by a hospital giving shock treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocking' looks like scandalous but is literal electric shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to bully or intimidate with blustering talk, which is to browbeat.

clue.text: Decorate Caruso's unfinished hotel

indicators.note: unfinished means the first name loses its final letter

parts.note: Enrico Caruso was the famous Italian tenor
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel named after the tenor Caruso is left half-decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts the O from ENRICO.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich can mean to adorn or embellish, as in enriching a building with ornament.

clue.text: Neck brace fitted after surgery — that's miserable

parts.note: to neck a drink is to down it in one
a plaster cast supports a limb after an operation

explanation.surface: A patient fitted with a neck brace after an operation feels wretched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neck' looks like the body part but is the verb meaning to swig.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast eyes look at the ground, so the word means dejected, low in spirits.

clue.text: Son with excessively twisted smutty material

indicators.note: twisted means turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: too means excessively

explanation.surface: A son with an overly twisted mind likes smutty stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smutty' suggests rude, but smut is literally sooty grime.
explanation.definitionFit: Soot is black dirt from burning, and smut is a flake of it, so it is smutty material.

clue.text: Benefit time went very quickly in recession

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: an era is a period of time
time flew means it went by fast

explanation.surface: Welfare payments and time flying by during an economic slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' reverses ERAFLEW as a whole. 'Recession' suggests the economy, which benefit payments fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Welfare is state financial support, what British English calls benefit.

clue.text: Emma's to do nowt to obstruct huge beast

indicators.note: to obstruct is to block, so the words surround and block in the answer

explanation.surface: Emma would do nothing to get in the way of an enormous animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nowt' is northern English for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastodon was a huge prehistoric elephant-like mammal, so it is a giant beast.

clue.text: Tragedy returning to celebrity magazine

indicators.note: returning means the little word comes back the other way

parts.note: Hello! is a celebrity gossip magazine

explanation.surface: A tragic story going back to the pages of a celebrity magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is one of Shakespeare's great tragedies, so it is an example of a tragedy.
